title: The Last Lonely Integer
statement: A positive integer $n$ is called lonely if there is exactly one ordered pair of positive integers $(a,b)$ with $a \le b$ and $5a+13b=n$. Find the largest lonely integer.
hints: Suppose $(a,b)$ satisfies $5a+13b=n$. Look for a way to change $a$ and $b$ so that the value of $5a+13b$ stays the same.

Use the general solution of a linear Diophantine equation. Since $\gcd(5,13)=1$, every integer solution of $5x+13y=n$ has the form $(a+13t,\,b-5t)$ for an integer $t$. Work out when the steps $t=1$ and $t=-1$ give another valid pair.

The step $(a-13,\,b+5)$ fails only if $a\le 13$, and the step $(a+13,\,b-5)$ fails only if $b\le a+17$. So a lonely integer must meet both conditions. Maximise $5a+13b$ under them, then check that the maximising pair really is the only pair for its value of $n$.
solution:
Solutions of $5a+13b=n$ form the family $(a+13t,\,b-5t)$, $t\in\mathbb Z$.

Let $n$ be lonely with pair $(a,b)$, $1\le a\le b$.

If $a\ge 14$, then $(a-13,b+5)$ is another valid pair, since $1\le a-13\le b+5$. So $a\le 13$.

If $b\ge a+18$, then $(a+13,b-5)$ is another valid pair, since $a+13\le b-5$. So $b\le a+17$.

Hence
$$n=5a+13b\le 18a+221\le 18\cdot 13+221=455.$$

For $n=455$, the pair $(13,30)$ works, since $65+390=455$. Every integer solution of $5x+13y=455$ is $(13+13t,\,30-5t)$, because $13\mid 5(x-13)$ and $\gcd(5,13)=1$. If $t\le -1$ then $x\le 0$. If $t\ge 1$ then $x\ge 26>25\ge y$. So only $t=0$ is valid, and $455$ is lonely. The answer is $455$.
